newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Strong U.S. jobs data push Swiss stocks lower.
newsitem.headline: Strong U.S. jobs data push Swiss stocks lower.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower on Friday, led down by stronger than expected U.S. December jobs data that sparked fears of a possible U.S. interest rate hike, dealers said.
Until the strong U.S. payrolls figures for December, the Swiss stock market had moved sideways.
Dealers said fears of rising interest rates pressured financial shares, while industrial stocks saw profit-taking.
Losses were mainly a consolidation of recent gains.
The SMI index of leading shares ended 18.8 points lower at 3,947.4. The all-share SPI fell 12.58 points to 2,526.61.
Turnover-leader Novartis bearers were one franc lower at 1,539 after coming off an earlier high at 1,550.
Dealers said trade was hectic at times after the U.S. data, with the SMI index slipping as low as 3,924.9. However, it recovered from lows towards the close.
Trade on the options and future exchange Soffex also picked up with U.S. data, with 184,809 options changing hands in a call-put ratio of 1.19 to one.

Winterthur calls were active with a turnover of 49,045 contracts. A dealer said he expected speculative demand was behind the high volume on the back of rumours Winterthur plans to cooperate with a German company.
Turnover in SMI futures was 6,576 contracts. A dealer said many players sold futures after the U.S. data to hedge positions.
